newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Christmas revelry in Bethlehem despite tensions.
newsitem.headline: Christmas revelry in Bethlehem despite tensions.

text.p: Thousands of pilgrims and revelers streamed into the PLO-ruled birthplace of Jesus on Christmas Day as residents praised the Palestinian Authority for putting a holiday shine on the West Bank town.

Even before the first morning bells summoned worshippers to Bethlehem's Church of the Nativity, neighbouring Manger Square had been scoured clean of the trash of the tens of thousands of merrymakers who jammed the courtyard on Christmas Eve.

"Last year it was a disaster area," an employee of a souvenir store told Reuters on Wednesday in a reference to the first Christmas under Palestinian self-rule. "This year the Authority organised themselves better."

The Christmas spirit passed over mostly Moslem Hebron, the nearby town where Israeli troops scuffled with Jewish settlers on rooftops and in the streets during protests against the expected handover of most of Hebron to the PLO.
Witnesses said Palestinians were apparently behind two firebomb attacks near a Jewish home in Hebron and on an Israeli military border police vehicle later.

The 400 settlers in the heart of the town of 100,000 Arabs fear Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu will harm their security if he agrees to hand over most Hebron to Palestinian self-rule. Israel and the PLO predict a deal could be reached in a week.
Palestinian Higher Education Minister Hanan Ashrawi said the tensions had dampened Bethlehem's second autonomous Christmas.

"It is somehow tarnished by the fact that all the hopes and expectations of last year have not been fulfilled yet," Ashrawi told Israel Radio. Israel withdrew from the town of 40,000 Moslem and Christian Arabs just before Christmas last year.
In Rome, Pope John Paul said his thoughts were with Bethlehem and all the Holy Land, entreating: "Hope must not die, despite provocations and profound differences."
Exuberant pilgrims were unfazed by regional volatility.
"Don't ask me about politics, it's all about peace and love, brother," shouted one Spanish tourist, adding: "Feliz Navidad!"
One Filipina pilgrim who said she had come to Bethlehem on Christmas for many years -- under both Israeli and Palestinian rule -- took a broader view.
"This city has passed through so many rulers since Jesus was born here. It will always be holy," Maya Balibolos said.
Palestinian merchants, who say simmering instability has kept tourists away despite Bethlehem's treasure trove of historic sites, were satisfied with the Christmas rush.

"This is the best Christmas in years. There were many people, many tourists. It was beautiful," Anton Antonio, owner of the Christmas Tree cafe, told said as a passing Santa Claus tossed candies to Palestinian children.
"Merry Christmas from Finland - where the real Santa Claus is coming from," chortled a Finn wearing a red fur cloak and hat in the Middle East town that has rarely known a white Christmas.
Asked how he could be sure the real Santa Claus came from Finland, he quipped: "Do you think my sleigh is pulled by camels?"
